evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Do you have any questions concerns about this move dates times furniture specific furniture items.' — asked before address/square-footage logistics probing began.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer answered 'No' to the formal concerns question — no-concern fix applied.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: N/A — Stage 3 treated as full credit; call correctly, cleanly hands off before pricing per the walkthrough-scheduler rule.

top_strength: Captured a full, room-by-room inventory (3 bedrooms, living room, patio set, garage, 3 TVs) in a single detailed pass with no need to circle back for missed items.
coaching_note: None of the three core differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) were mentioned anywhere in this call — a real gap, since it's a full 12-minute discovery conversation and there was ample room to work them in even though pricing itself gets handled by a specialist.
grading_notes: Judgment call: classified as walkthrough_scheduler and applied Stage 3 N/A/full credit even though this is a phone handoff to an internal large-move specialist rather than a literal virtual walkthrough appointment. The home is 3000 sq ft (well over the >=1800 sq ft threshold the rubric uses for this treatment), and the handoff was clean and by-design ('I am going to get this over to the specialist who does a bit of a larger move... do you mind if I give you a call back?' — customer agreed) rather than an abandoned or confused mid-pitch trail-off, so the spirit of the walkthrough-scheduler rule was applied by extension. Stage 1/2 items were still scored normally per the rubric's explicit instruction that discovery and differentiators always apply.
